newsitem.title: USA: CEFTA gives US firms "export platforms" - official.
newsitem.headline: CEFTA gives US firms "export platforms" - official.

text.p: U.S. companies can use CEFTA as an "export platform" back to the European Union, said Stuart Eizenstat, U.S. Undesecretary of Commerce.

Speaking at the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) conference here on Monday, Eizenstat said the agreement between CEFTA and the European Union (EU) to reduce tariffs on industrial goods opens the opportunity for U.S. companies operating in the region to export goods and services to the European Union.
"Frankly it is difficult for us at the Commerce Department to envision U.S. companies having an integrated corporate strategy for Europe without considering the CEFTA countries," he said.

CEFTA comprises Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia. Romania is scheduled to join CEFTA in July. The CEFTA countries represent a market totalling $570 billion in terms of "purchasing power parity," Eizenstat said.
U.S. companies "awakened earlier" than European companies to the fact that the CEFTA region is a good place to invest and do business, Eizenstat said.
American firms have invested more than $9.0 billion in the CEFTA countries, or about 25 percent of total foreign direct investment, he said.
But the total U.S. export to CEFTA countries totals only about $2.0 billion, or 3.0 percent of CEFTA's imports from the OECD countries, he said.

Eizenstat said half of U.S. investment in Central Europe is in Hungary and "if the region as a whole had attracted as much investment per capita as Hungary, total U.S. investment in the CEFTA region would have been $30 billion."
U.S. products have faced "negative tariff differentials" vis-a-vis EU products as the CEFTA countries have implemented their EU association agreements, Eizenstat said.
"We have begun discussing this with CEFTA members and hope to see all of CEFTA's tariffs falling rapidly to the level of the EU's rates," he said.
Eizenstat urged the CEFTA countries to harmonize their countries' standards systems with the U.S. system.
"In our vision, CEFTA will create a single Central European market which will be far greater than the sum of its parts," he said.
The CEFTA conference, the first in the United States, is organized by the Business Council for International Understanding (BCIU).
